newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish exports rose 10 pct in March - exporters.
newsitem.headline: Turkish exports rose 10 pct in March - exporters.

text.p: Turkish exports rose by 10 percent to $2.30 billion in March from $2.09 billion in the same 1996 period, led by a 20 percent rise in the leading readywear exports, the Turkish Exporters' Assembly (TIM) said on Thursday.
TIM chairman Okan Oguz said in a statement that lower 1996 export figures and easing recession in Turkey's main trade partners Germany and the European Union (EU) were major factors behind the rise.
Oguz also said Turkey's exports to the United States also picked up after last year's drop.

Compared to March 1996, readywear exports leapt 20 percent to $655.03 million, iron and non-iron exports edged up three percent to $292.84 million, textile and related raw material exports rose 10 percent to $246.34 million, electric-electronic exports grew five percent to $171.02 million and grains, pulses and oilseed exports jumped 24 percent to $160.57 million in March 1997.
TIM reported a 15 percent decline in automotive and parts exports to $130.51 million.

In January, Turkey's exports fell 1.2 percent to $1.7 billion while imports rose 10.2 percent to $3.3 billion and the trade deficit jumped 25.6 percent to $1.6 billion, compared to a year ago, according to official data.
